statusNote: Founded 1941 as National School of Business; acquired by Harold D. Buckingham in 1962 and renamed National American University in 1997. The physical Rapid City campus closed in 2019 as NAU consolidated to a mostly online delivery model (it retained small on-base sites at Ellsworth AFB, SD and Kings Bay, GA). As of the 2024-2025 catalog the institution is still operating online under Higher Learning Commission accreditation, though enrollment has fallen sharply (~1,600 students) and NAU Holdings (OTC: NAUH) has faced financial distress and Heightened Cash Monitoring status from the Dept. of Education. Named president/CEO succession for 1996-2009 could not be reliably documented; founder-owner Harold D. Buckingham led the institution from 1962 until his death in 1995, and the Buckingham family has remained involved as chairman/board members since.

leaders.priorTitle: Various internal leadership roles (faculty, financial aid administration)
leaders.notes: Joined NAU in 1991 as a Student Account Specialist, rose through financial aid administration and faculty roles (accounting/finance, 1995-2002), and was named System CEO in 2009 and President & CEO in January 2016. Oversaw NAU Holdings' 2010 NASDAQ IPO, the 2019 shift away from physical campuses (including the Rapid City campus closure), and the company's later move to OTC markets amid financial strain. No other named president/CEO of NAU could be confirmed for 1996-2009.

statusNote: Also operates a campus in Tampa, FL, and acquired Kendall College (Chicago) in 2018. Complete presidential records between Orley Herron's departure (~1998-1999) and Nivine Megahed's 2010 arrival could not be reliably confirmed via public sources; NLU counts Megahed as its 11th president, implying at least one additional president/leader served in that gap whose name and dates were not identifiable in this research pass.

leaders.notes: Led the institution (then National College of Education, renamed National Louis University in 1990) through a reported 22-year tenure marked by major campus expansion (six Illinois campuses, five out-of-state centers, and operations in four European countries). Start/end years are inferred from his reported 22-year tenure following 7 years as Greenville's president starting 1970; not independently confirmed. Died in 2019 at age 85.

11th president. A clinical psychologist by training, she previously led the University of Sarasota and Kendall College (which NLU later acquired in 2018). Took over in March 2010 during the Great Recession, when NLU's revenue had dropped roughly 30% and the board reportedly weighed closing the university; credited with a financial and enrollment turnaround (Undergraduate College, School of Nursing, Kendall acquisition, expanded online programming). Announced her retirement effective the end of the 2025-26 academic year.

12th president, taking office August 1, 2026, during NLU's 140th anniversary year; NLU's first Black president. Joined NLU in 2021 as Vice Provost of Academic Programs and Accreditation and became Provost/SVP in 2022. Previously held roles at Kennedy-King College, Northern Illinois University, Malcolm X College, and Rush University Medical Center.

statusNote: Founded in 1996 in Prescott Valley, AZ as a for-profit online graduate university. Acquired by the nonprofit National University System (headquartered in La Jolla, CA) in 2019, converting it to nonprofit status, and formally merged into National University in fall 2022 -- Northcentral no longer operates as a separately accredited institution; its academic programs continue under the National University banner. Leadership between founder Donald Hecht's tenure and George Burnett's ~2011 appointment is not fully documented in public sources and may include an unidentified interim leader or gap.

leaders.notes: Founded Northcentral University in 1996 in Prescott Valley, Arizona as an online doctoral/graduate university. End year as president is inferred around the October 2008 sale of a majority ownership stake to Rockbridge Growth Equity, LLC and Falcon Investments, LLC; not independently confirmed. He remained a minority owner afterward and later founded/led California Southern University.

Start year (2011) is approximate/best-available. Led Northcentral through its transition from for-profit private-equity ownership to acquisition by the nonprofit National University System in 2019. Later became president of University of Phoenix in February 2022 but resigned within months amid Dept. of Education scrutiny over his prior oversight of Westwood College, which had been found to have deceived students about job prospects.

Rose internally at NCU from faculty scholar to general counsel to provost before being named president upon the National University System's completed acquisition in January 2019. Continued as president through Northcentral's fall 2022 merger into National University, and remains in a leadership role as the two institutions' academic structures continue to consolidate as of 2025-26.

unit: College of Professional Studies (formerly University College / School of Professional and Continuing Studies)
statusNote: This is not a separately chartered institution but Northeastern University's continuing/professional-education unit -- known as University College through 2003, School of Professional and Continuing Studies from 2003-2014, and the College of Professional Studies (CPS) from 2014 onward. It is led by a Dean who reports to Northeastern's overall President; Joseph E. Aoun has served as Northeastern University's president since 2006, spanning the entire leaders list below. Dean coverage for roughly 2003-2010 (between Judith Stoessel's interim term and John LaBrie's 2010 appointment) could not be reliably confirmed and is flagged as a gap.

leaders.notes: Dean of University College at Northeastern from 1978 until 1997; this entry begins at the 1996 research-window start though his tenure began earlier and is outside this index's scope.
Served as interim dean of University College between Jordan and Zaborowski.
Held the combined title of Vice Provost for Adult and Continuing Education and Dean, University College.
Interim dean during the period University College was renamed School of Professional and Continued Studies (2003). Successor coverage from 2003-2010 could not be confirmed.

leaders.nextRole: Founding Principal, Northeastern University Toronto Campus
leaders.notes: Dean of the College of Professional Studies and VP for Professional Education, May 2010-May 2016; more than doubled CPS's annual revenue budget (from $65M to $140M) and grew international enrollment 95% in five years. Moved internally in 2016 to found Northeastern's Toronto regional campus.

Served as interim dean starting May 2016 (after LaBrie moved to found the Toronto campus) and was named permanent dean in April 2017. An English professor and Northeastern faculty member since 1988. Left in March 2023 to become dean of Cornell's School of Continuing Education.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior academic/faculty leadership role, College of Professional Studies
leaders.notes: Named interim dean in December 2023 following Loeffelholz's departure, then appointed permanent dean in January 2025. A Northeastern faculty member for over a decade prior to becoming dean.
